_provenance.supersedes: The five impact claims, eleven KPIs and six expected-impact mappings of the Master Draft configuration. The Pack's §2.3 carries four impact blocks and — new — the evidence-based magnitude context that closes the open-decisions section-4 question. KPIs are re-anchored to the new deliverable set (operator ruling 2026-08-28); the KPI discipline (each KPI measures something the project controls and delivers; no advance numeric water-saving promises) carries over unchanged.
_provenance.kpi_note: K1-K11 below are the operator's re-anchoring of the accepted KPI pattern onto the Pack deliverables, recorded in the baseline decision log. Each names one deliverable that exists in workpackage_seed.json so phase_05_gate predicate g06_p05 can resolve traceable_to_deliverable.

impacts.title: Scientific impact
impacts.claim: FIELDWISE provides a validation framework in which operationally obtainable data streams are judged against independent plant-level ground truth and challenged under both unseen-year and new commercial-field conditions. It clarifies which stress relationships survive the transition from proximal measurements toward UAV and Sentinel-2 field monitoring and which components of the modelling/decision workflow are genuinely reusable beyond the development crop — a methodological basis for later crop-by-crop extension across irrigated high-value horticulture rather than unsupported universalisation from tomato.

impacts.title: Agricultural and environmental impact
impacts.claim: FIELDWISE starts with processing tomato because the consortium can build on approximately five years of heterogeneous scientific observations (2022-2026); the intended application domain is irrigated high-value horticulture. The project will not promise a fixed percentage reduction in irrigation water, because actual savings depend on crop, cultivar, soil, weather, growth stage, irrigation system and the management action taken. Published processing-tomato evidence provides credible magnitude context (see impact_magnitude_evidence); project-specific water saving, yield, quality and uncertainty are reported from the prospective validation data.

impacts.title: Technological and economic impact
impacts.claim: The web-based DrR MVP provides a tangible route from validated research to external testing, preserving the distinction between the fellow's pre-existing DrR background and FIELDWISE foreground. The architecture is crop-configurable: processing tomato supplies the first validated crop module; reusable data-ingestion, uncertainty, visualisation and irrigation-attention components can support later modules after crop-specific validation. AgroVIR identifies the data, usability, interoperability and workflow requirements for future FMIS integration; Krumatic supports software implementation and Bulgarian farmer-facing uptake. Economic value is not expressed as an invented EUR/ha promise; FIELDWISE quantifies irrigation water applied, water productivity, yield/marketable yield, quality indicators, intervention timing, warning lead time and operational requirements from which later economic value can be assessed.

impacts.title: European and societal relevance
impacts.claim: Eurostat reports fresh vegetables cultivated over approximately 2.0 million hectares in the EU in 2023, and about 0.7 million EU farms cultivating fresh vegetables in the 2020 census — the scale of the horticultural domain in which scientifically transferable plant-based irrigation decision support could ultimately matter, not an immediate market. Bulgaria provides concrete downstream context: 35.6 thousand hectares of main vegetable area and about 128 thousand tonnes of tomato in harvest 2024. The combination of Hungarian scientific and industrial environments, a real farmer validation setting, Bulgarian software/dissemination links and a defined post-MSCA MVCRI replication route provides a realistic pathway toward wider reuse. FIELDWISE contributes particularly to SDG 2, SDG 6, SDG 12 and SDG 13.

impact_magnitude_evidence.note: Closes the open-decisions section-4 question (review finding F-4 / action A-1): bounded, literature-referenced magnitude context, never a project promise. Full bibliographic entries are in source_materials/references/fieldwise_references.bib (R36-R40).
impact_magnitude_evidence.source_ref: Pack E (evidence table); Pack §2.3; Pack 'Selected references supporting the impact magnitude context'
impact_magnitude_evidence.adopted_claim_form: Comparable published studies demonstrate water-saving effects in the approximate 8-30% range under specific strategies, but FIELDWISE will quantify its own outcome prospectively and report water saving together with yield, quality and uncertainty. The proposal must not write 'FIELDWISE will save 25% water.'

reference_points.evidence: Processing tomato, plant + soil monitoring: ~30% less irrigation water vs empirical farmer management; ~7.5% less vs ET-based scheduling in a two-year field trial; yield differences also reported.
reference_points.use: Bounded context only; demonstrates plausible magnitude and the need to quantify water-yield trade-offs.
reference_points.citation: Carucci et al. 2023, Applied Sciences 13, 7625, doi:10.3390/app13137625

reference_points.evidence: Processing tomato, timing of deficit: 25% water saving with early-stage controlled deficit without statistically significant yield loss; poorly timed/prolonged deficits reduced yield.
reference_points.use: Supports the plant-stage/physiology-aware timing premise; not a project promise.
reference_points.citation: Badr et al. 2026, BMC Plant Biology 26, 169, doi:10.1186/s12870-025-08065-6

reference_points.evidence: EU scale: fresh vegetables on ~2.0 million ha in the EU in 2023; ~0.7 million EU farms cultivated fresh vegetables in 2020.
reference_points.use: Scale of the potential application domain, not an immediate addressable market.
reference_points.citation: Eurostat 2024 (Key figures on the European food chain); Eurostat 2025 (The fruit and vegetable sector in the EU)

reference_points.evidence: Bulgaria scale: 35.6 thousand ha main vegetable-production area in harvest 2024; ~128 thousand tonnes tomato production.
reference_points.citation: Ministry of Agriculture and Food, Bulgaria, 2025, No. 452

kpis.note: Eleven KPIs re-anchored to the Pack deliverable set by the operator ruling of 2026-08-28 (baseline record), preserving the accepted discipline: each measures something the project controls and delivers; none promises a numeric water saving in advance. Every deliverable in workpackage_seed.json has at least one KPI tracing to it.
kpis.source_ref: decision_log/fieldwise-run-02-baseline_2026-08-28.json (KPI re-anchoring); pattern from operator input pack item 5 and AR-5/AR-10

items.title: Harmonised archive coverage
items.target: The 2022-2026 seasons integrated into the common-variable matrix with documented QC flags, missingness/measurement-frequency map and metadata

items.title: Stress target and validation design predefined
items.target: Primary physiological stress target, corroborating endpoints, feature-selection rules and blocked temporal validation criteria published in the protocol before modelling begins

items.title: Released model documented
items.target: Primary model and nonlinear benchmark (where justified) reported with calibration, uncertainty and blocked unseen-year performance in one model card

items.title: Crop-transfer specification stated
items.target: Transferable core components, crop-specific parameters, minimum validation dataset and recalibration gates enumerated for adding a new crop

items.title: Independent validation dataset delivered
items.target: A prospective commercial-field dataset with continuous environmental record, documented irrigation timing/amounts, and reference physiological measurements per protocol

items.title: Transfer gap quantified
items.target: Prospective performance, uncertainty and any limited recalibration reported against the predefined criteria; transfer loss stated, not hidden

items.title: MVP delivered
items.target: Web MVP reachable and serving field-level stress probability/class, uncertainty/confidence, temporal trend and an irrigation-attention output (LOW/MONITOR/HIGH/URGENT) for the validated tomato module

items.title: Pre-placement readiness dossier
items.target: External access tested and the M25-M30 evaluation protocol with usability/interoperability requirements documented before the placement begins

items.title: External evaluation completed
items.target: The AgroVIR assessment covers MVP inputs, usability, missing-data behaviour, decision outputs, workflow compatibility and interoperability requirements

items.title: Integration path defined
items.target: The FMIS roadmap names the required interfaces, the exploitation route and the post-fellowship steps

items.title: Career Development Plan agreed and reviewed
items.target: Career Development Plan agreed by M3 and reviewed at all five steering points (M6, M14, M18, M24, M27)

expected_impact_coverage.note: phase_05_gate predicate g06_p04 requires every Tier 2B expected impact to carry at least one mapped project output. All six map under the ATK-hosted configuration; the EI-06 route is superseded (teaching route decision, decision_log/fieldwise-run02-supersessions_2026-08-28.json).

mappings.expected_impact: Improved employability and career prospects of researchers within academia and beyond.
mappings.mapped_measure: The Agricultural-Data-Scientist progression of Pack §1.4/§2.1, made operational by the Career Development Plan (D1.3) and the inter-sectoral AgroVIR placement (M25-M30), which supplies operational model evaluation, research-to-MVP translation, agricultural-software requirements and exploitation planning.

mappings.expected_impact: Strengthened international, inter-sectoral and interdisciplinary research collaboration.
mappings.mapped_measure: International: the Hungary-Bulgaria bridge (Krumatic in-action; MVCRI post-MSCA replication route). Inter-sectoral: AgroVIR consultation and placement, Krumatic development seat. Interdisciplinary: the two-way transfer between plant physiology/horticulture and modelling/EO/data science of Pack §1.3.

mappings.expected_impact: Broadened public engagement with research and innovation.
mappings.mapped_measure: Practitioner-oriented demonstrations of stress/uncertainty outputs; Krumatic-supported farmer-facing demonstrations and communication in Bulgaria; one public-facing article per year (operator-preserved measure); the possible Szentendre Skanzen public-facing demonstration linking traditional horticultural knowledge with modern sensing, only if the garden is formally established and suitable.
mappings.source_ref: Pack §2.2; operator-preserved measure from input pack item 5 (EI-03)
mappings.note: Carries no deliverable id: no deliverable covers it and inventing one would fabricate a project fact. Phase 5 may propose a dissemination deliverable; Phase 3 owns the deliverable list.

mappings.expected_impact: Enhanced convergence of researcher working conditions with the European Charter for Researchers.
mappings.mapped_measure: Charter alignment evidenced at instrument level by the Career Development Plan (D1.3) and by the supervision and training arrangements of Pack §1.3 under the re-anchored governance. No institutional HR award is claimed for ATK: its HRS4R status has not been established, and the HRS4R prohibition pattern of the prior configuration (no unverified accreditation claims) governs.
mappings.source_ref: Pack §1.3; operator input pack item 5 pattern (C8), re-anchored 2026-08-28
mappings.note: The thinnest mapping, as before. If ATK is found to hold the HR Excellence in Research award, the claim may be added on evidence; it must not be assumed.

mappings.expected_impact: Increased R&I capacity, output and knowledge transfer among European research organisations.
mappings.mapped_measure: The model card, the crop-transfer specification and the prospective transferability report, together with the §1.3 two-way transfer between the fellow and the ATK/ELTE/MATE environments and the P1-P2 publications (a third methods/application paper if the independent dataset supports it).

mappings.expected_impact: Enhanced integration of research results into higher education and teaching at host organisations.
mappings.mapped_measure: Short guest lectures, seminars or practical sessions at MATE and, where institutionally possible, the Agricultural University of Plovdiv, linking plant-stress physiology with UAV/EO monitoring, precision agriculture and agricultural data science — transferring the fellow's five years of university teaching into the new discipline. SUPERSEDES the ELTE MSc module unit and PhD co-supervision measures of the prior configuration, which fell with the university host.
mappings.note: Like EI-03, carries no deliverable id. The route is concrete despite ATK being a research organisation rather than a university, which Pack §1.3 addresses explicitly.
